newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Dollar vols ease in Europe, spot steadier.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dollar vols ease in Europe, spot steadier.

text.p: Dollar option volatilities started lower in morning Europe as the dollar/yen spot rate steadied after its recent decline and dollar/mark edged back above Monday's lows.

Dollar/yen implied volatilities were marked lower, with one-month vol now at 13.4/13.8 percent compared with late Monday's 14.5/14.9 percent. One-week volatility stood at 15.0/16.5 percent against 18.0/20.0.
"Vols are very sensitive to spot moves at the moment and we should see levels come off more as long as spot holds above 112 yen, or at least yesterday's lows," said a U.S. bank options dealer.

The dollar/yen spot rate shed almost four yen from late Friday trade to early Monday in Asia, mainly amid fresh concerns over the growing Japanese-U.S. trade gap. Dollar/yen spot was trading at 112.84/89 at 0822 GMT against 112.65/75 late Monday.
Although spot steadied somewhat by morning Europe, dealers said the risk was still firmly on the downside and noted overnight buying interest in risk reversals.
The one-month risk reversal, the difference in implied volatility of calls relative to puts, steepened its bias to yen calls and stood at 1.8/2.1 from late Monday's European level of 1.5/1.9.
Dollar/mark vols were more subdued, easing back slightly as the spot rate held above 1.71 marks, up from late Monday's level of 1.7055/60.

Dealers said confusion over the dollar's direction amid the ongoing concerns over Europe's monetary union timetable are likely to keep dollar/mark and EMS currency vols bid, at least until the outcome of this Friday's Franco-German summit meeting.

Option vols were bid up in dollar/mark and on the mark crosses Monday after France called for a delay in its agreement of the EMU budget stability pact. While this is seen increasing the chances of an EMU delay, French and other European politicians are insisting on a timely start.
Dollar/mark vols were trading at 9.35/9.65 percent, slightly easier from late Monday's 9.6/9.9 percent. Dollar direction was neutral and the risk reversal remained unchanged around par.
Mark cross volatilities remained bid but slightly below Monday levels. Mark/Paris one-month was trading at 2.0/2.3 percent against 2.1/2.6 while mark/lira stood at 5.05/5.55 against 5.4/5.8 percent.
